statements.proposition: This change preserves the pre-existing timeout logic (userTimeout + waitFor + actionWaitTime + 5000ms), so request timeouts are backward compatible.
statements.label: FALSE
statements.note: At the base commit the JS SDK had no waitFor/action-wait summation: v1 used timeout + 5000 only (postRequest: data.timeout + 5000; scrapeUrl: params.timeout + 5000), and v2 HttpClient used a fixed per-client axios timeout (options.timeoutMs ?? 60000) with no per-request calculation. The change introduces new arithmetic (adds waitFor and action wait times; in v2 a request without timeout now gets 60000 + waits, overriding a client-level timeoutMs). So the logic is not 'the same' as before. Possible that the author meant parity with another SDK; not observable as preserved in this repository's JS code.
evidence: gh api repos/firecrawl/firecrawl/pulls/2201/files: 1 added test file, 8 modified files under apps/js-sdk/firecrawl/src (v1/index.ts, v2/methods/*.ts, v2/utils/httpClient.ts)

Base 606d50b grep of apps/js-sdk/firecrawl/src for 5000|actionWait|milliseconds: only 'params.timeout + 5000' and 'data.timeout + 5000' in v1/index.ts (and index.backup.ts); no waitFor or action-wait summation
Base v2/utils/httpClient.ts: timeout only in axios.create({timeout: options.timeoutMs ?? 60000}); post/get/delete take no timeout
Head v2/utils/httpClient.ts calculateTimeout returns timeoutMs + waits + 5000, or 60000 + waits when timeoutMs undefined; head v1 calculateTotalTimeout adds waitFor + action waits to timeout + 5000
